purpose: Assesses whether the organization can prevent or detect an adversary gaining higher-level permissions on systems or networks that host or interact with AI resources.
summary: Privilege Escalation consists of techniques adversaries use to gain higher-level permissions on a system or network, often after entering with unprivileged access. Common approaches take advantage of system weaknesses, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities. Examples of elevated access include SYSTEM/root level, local administrator, or accounts with admin-like access to AI-specific systems or functions.
expectedStatementElements: How least-privilege access is enforced for accounts and service principals interacting with AI systems and infrastructure
What controls prevent misuse of valid credentials to escalate privileges within AI pipelines (training, deployment, inference)
How the organization detects unusual privilege escalation attempts on systems hosting AI artifacts
Whether privilege boundaries between development, staging, and production AI environments are enforced
evidenceExamples: Least-privilege access control policy and role definitions for AI infrastructure and pipelines
Privileged access monitoring/alerting for AI training, deployment, and inference systems
Environment segregation documentation between dev/staging/production AI systems
Periodic access review records for elevated-privilege AI system accounts
commonGaps: Service accounts used in AI pipelines run with far broader permissions than the pipeline actually requires
No monitoring exists for privilege escalation attempts specific to AI infrastructure
Development and production AI environments share credentials or lack clear privilege boundaries
interviewQuestions: Do our AI pipeline service accounts run with only the permissions they actually need, or broader?
Would we notice if someone tried to escalate privileges on a system hosting our AI models?
Are our development and production AI environments truly separated in terms of access?
When was the last time we reviewed who has elevated access to our AI infrastructure?
